body: Pre-registered 2026-11-24 (research_notes/Backtests/survival_cap_general_india.md). Sample E (2018-25 firm-quarter events, non-financial, 1,975 flagged / 6,822 not, 481 firms): 12-month halving 17.8% vs 7.1%, RR 2.49 [1.96, 3.13] firm-cluster bootstrap (P1 pass; not blind - implied by earlier A-D groups); 3-yr failure 14.4% vs 2.7%, RR 5.24 [3.26, 8.60]; 3x winners in 3 yrs 21.3% vs 15.6%, RR 1.37 [1.05, 1.75]; 3-yr mean excess +18.4 pp [-11.3, +52.9] (median worse: -41% vs -34%). Sample P (survivorship-free 2016/18 snapshots, weighted, blind): 5-yr failure 2.36x [1.58, 3.66] (P2 pass), 12-month halving 1.43x [0.90, 2.30] (not), 5-yr winners 0.91x. Winner cost: cap flags 22.5% of events but 30.7% of 3x winner events and 63% of failures; 39 of 190 winner firms (21%) flagged at every winning entry; in P 27% of winners vs 29% of firms. Pledge is bad on both tails (P: winners 0.55x, 3-yr excess -42 pp); interest cover is a variance flag. S1/S5 not testable incrementally (8 events), no signal alone - not triggers. Decision per rule: ADOPT general cap = starter size (1%), no additions, balance-sheet question; PEAD window + flag stays 0 new money. Card change proposed (not applied): survival_cap_general_outputs/proposed_card_v1.3.diff. Research, not SEBI-registered advice.
title: Back-test: general survival cap (pledge>25% or interest cover<1.5x, any SUE) — ADOPT as starter-size cap; flagged firms are high-variance
